references.view: Close daytime exterior confirms stone shaft, projecting four-sided clock stage, convex mansard crown and small lantern. Not the Palais de Justice clock tower.

licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
assistance: AI-assisted architectural interpretation and procedural recipe authoring; deterministic Python/Blender export. No photographic textures.
modelingNotes: The clock tower is modeled independently of Gare de Lyon. OSM supplies the 35–50 m clock stage, 63 m main roof and 67 m lantern. The main roof part starts at ground in the source; the outline fills the remaining lower shaft to 35 m.

The inspected close view shows four large circular dials, a heavy cornice, curved mansard crown and small lantern. A shared faceted dome profile approximates the convex main crown within its mapped plan; 3.2 m clock radius, 42.5 m clock centers and cornice thickness are visual inferences.

The 35 m lower-shaft fill is an explicit interpretation of the floating clock-stage minimum height and the observed continuous shaft. Dial marks use existing clock primitives; sculptures and fine roof ornament are omitted.
